To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heat shock response is induced by the HSFs and that it is required for the maintenance of protein homeostasis in cells.

the heat shock response, which plays a major role to maintain protein homeo‐stasis, is regulated by a set of HSFs and that the heat shock genes are classified into classical heat shock genes that are induced by all HSFs and nonclassical heat‐induced genes that are induced only by some of the HSFs.
HSF1, HSF2, HSF3 and HSF4 play a role in the expression of nonclassical as well as classical heat shock genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of nonclassical HSF‐inducible heat shock genes and the elucidation of their biological functions.
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms underlying the heat shock response, which is a key process for adaptation to protein misfolding and for maintaining protein homeostatis.
the identification and analysis of HSF‐dependent heat shock genes, and with elucidating the role of these genes in the heat shock response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HSFs are master regulators of heat shock genes, including the classical and the nonclassical ones.
HSFs are essential for adaptation to proteotoxic stresses.
the HSF family plays an important role in adaptation to proteotoxic stresses by regulating the expression of both classical and nonclassical heat‐inducable heat shock genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HSF family regulates a set of heat shock genes, which are required to protect cells from heat shock.
the heat shock response is a complex system in which HSFs induce both classical and nonclassical heat‐inducibile genes to protect cells against proteotoxic stress.

the heat shock response is an adaptation mechanism to proteotoxic stress, which is mediated by the HSF‐dependent expression of heat shock proteins and other proteins that are required for maintaining protein homeostases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

HSFs are not only master regulators of classical heat shock proteins, but also play a major role in regulating the expression of nonclassical genes, which might be required for the adaptation to proteotoxic stresses.

HSF1, HSF2, HSF3 and HSF4 are required for the induction of nonclassical as well as classical heat shock genes, which are involved in protein folding and suppression of protein aggregation, respectively, to maintain protein homeo‐stasis.

the heat shock response plays a significant role in the maintenance of protein homeostasis and that the induction of classical and nonclassical heat‐inducibles is required for the protection of cells and organisms from proteotoxic stress.
